From the Moon to the time on your clock

Follow sunlight from lunar phases to Earth’s seasons, then separate the motion of Earth from the rules on our clocks.

By Biel Sardà · Published 30 Sept 2026 · Suggest a correction

What you will learn

Start with something you can notice in the sky: the Moon seems to change shape. Build a picture of sunlight and motion, then use it to understand seasons and the human choices behind civil time.

Before you start: No astronomy background needed. The last lesson includes simple clock arithmetic.

  • Explain lunar phases without confusing them with eclipses.
  • Connect seasons to tilt, sunlight angle and daylight.
  • Distinguish a time zone from its current UTC offset.

Keep these ideas handy

Phase
The changing portion of the Moon’s illuminated half visible from Earth.
Axial tilt
The inclination of Earth’s rotation axis relative to its orbital plane.
UTC offset
The difference between a local clock and UTC at a particular moment.
